proof:
# A quantitative cap-centroid bound from its section mass

Let K be a d-dimensional convex body, d>=1, of volume V. Let u be a
unit normal and let the cap {u.x>=t} have volume 0<p<V and section
(d-1)-volume S>0. Write m=u.g_K-t for its ordinary centroid margin.
Then

    S m <= d p [1-(d/(d+1))(V/p)^(1/d)].                (1)

Applying (1) to the opposite cap also gives

    S m >= -d (V-p)[1-(d/(d+1))(V/(V-p))^(1/d)].       (2)

In particular m>=0 in (1) gives p>=gamma_d V. This recovers the
ordinary Grunbaum constant, while retaining the exact section slope.

Proof. Translate the threshold to zero, and put

    F(s)=|K intersect {u.x>=s}|.

Its d-th root is concave on its positive region by Brunn-Minkowski,
and F'(0)=-S. Its tangent line therefore gives

    F(s)<=p[1-Ss/(dp)]^d

where the right side has a nonnegative bracket; the positive cap cannot
extend beyond dp/S. Hence the positive first moment is bounded by

    integral_0^infinity F(s) ds <= d p^2/((d+1)S).

For negative thresholds write s=-r. Put

    r_0=(dp/S)[(V/p)^(1/d)-1].

On 0<=r<=r_0 the same tangent bound gives

    |K intersect {u.x<=-r}|=V-F(-r)
          >=V-p[1+Sr/(dp)]^d.

Integrating this lower bound for the negative first moment and subtracting
it from the preceding upper bound gives

 V m <= d p^2/((d+1)S)
       -(dp/S){ V[(V/p)^(1/d)-1]
          -p[(V/p)^((d+1)/d)-1]/(d+1)}
      =(d p V/S)[1-(d/(d+1))(V/p)^(1/d)].

Division by V proves (1); reflection proves (2). All integrals are over
a bounded support, and hyperplane boundaries have zero d-volume.

The inequality extends to a supporting facet by limits. At the upper
support p=0 its right side is interpreted as zero, while the centroid
margin is nonpositive. At the lower support p=V its right side is
dV/(d+1). The limiting facet section gives (1), and replacing its measure
by an effective density theta between zero and one preserves the inequality
because its centroid margin is then nonnegative. A saturated cap whose
effective section is zero is also covered by this interpretation.

## A scalar necessary condition in the selector system

For one of the proper active caps in
`candidate dcde24475c7f190c`, write its cap
volumes as p_A,p_B,p_C, its equal endpoint section masses as s>0,
and k=S_B/s>=1. Let

    Psi_V(p)=p-(d/(d+1)) V^(1/d) p^(1-1/d),

with its continuous endpoint value at p=0 for d>1. For d=1 the
proper-cap formula is Psi_V(p)=p-V/2. Let m_A,m_B,m_C be the margins
of the three ordinary centroids. Applying (1) gives

    a m_A+b m_B+a m_C
       <= (d/s){a[Psi_a(p_A)+Psi_c(p_C)]
                            +(b/k)Psi_b(p_B)}.          (3)

Here k>=1 follows from a dominated midpoint law for the equal-mass
endpoint effective sections, supported in the uniform central section.
The cap-volume identity is p_A+p_B+p_C=D.

In the nonzero selector-normal case, lower-cap ordering and the selected
centroid identity give

    sum_j rho_j[a m_Aj+b m_Bj+a m_Cj]>=0,
    rho_j=omega_j S_total,j.

Thus (3), summed with these positive rho_j, is an explicit scalar
necessary condition whenever all endpoint sections in question are
proper and positive. Cases s=0 must be retained separately; dividing by
s silently would discard exactly the central-only caps used in the
counterexample to the entire selector body.

No claim that this scalar condition forces the OC cap budget is made.
The selector-body obstruction shows that a universal implication of that
kind, if it included all zero-section cases, would be false.
